verification_strategy.module_checks: Future isolated checks shall exercise request storage, selection, command sequencing, timing enforcement, bank state, functional memory/response handling, host protocol behavior, and refresh behavior through declared interfaces after decomposition.
verification_strategy.system_scenario: Future system checks shall cover reset, consecutive admissions, FIFO ordering, full-queue simultaneous dispatch/admission, row hit/conflict behavior, timing boundaries, read/write ordering, refresh drain/service/resume, response timing, and diagnostic cmd_ready behavior.
verification_strategy.system_evidence: Future downstream evidence shall use independent admission, dispatch, command-commit, memory, response, timing, and refresh scoreboards/monitors. No downstream verification or backend stage has been executed.

D_RESET_STYLE.reason: Satisfies the synchronous reset requirement while retaining the stated reuse allowance.

D_RESPONSE_EDGE.reason: Defines the one-cycle response stage without another response adapter stage.

D_REFRESH_ORDER.reason: Resolves refresh preparation ordering and all-bank closure.

A_CLOCK_CONTINUES.statement: clk continues through reset and reset is sampled at at least one rising edge when state clearing is required.

A_HOST_STABILITY.statement: The host holds txn_valid and all request payload fields stable during any cycle in which txn_valid is asserted and txn_ready is low.

A_HOST_RESPONSE_SAMPLING.statement: The host samples every rsp_valid pulse; no response-ready or response-backpressure signal exists.

A_EVENTUAL_PROGRESS.statement: Eventual completion requires future legal command opportunities and clock progress; no fixed host-visible latency bound is specified.

A_REFRESH_MODEL.statement: The refresh behavior is a functional periodic pending/drain/service model and is not a claim of complete physical DDR4 refresh-debt behavior.

Q_EXPORT_APPROVAL.question: Approval tied to the exact reviewed specification package is required before RTL generation.

requirements.text: Implement global FIFO service in acceptance order, including same-address writes and reads. Admit on every rising-edge txn_valid && txn_ready, independently of command readiness.

Provide four waiting entries plus one separately stored active request. Dispatch only previously stored requests, capture the complete pre-edge head before releasing its slot, and permit full-queue simultaneous dispatch/admission including capacity one. No empty-queue bypass or same-edge active replacement at retirement.

Use explicit NOP/ACT/PRE/READ/WRITE/REF command semantics, with NOP never committed and at most one command commit per edge. Sequence closed banks with ACT-access, row hits with access, and row conflicts with PRE-ACT-access. PRE/ACT never retire the active request. Keep blocked candidates stable through stalls and newly pending refresh.

Keep separate owners for host mapping, waiting storage, scheduling, command sequencing, row state, timing, functional memory/responses, and refresh control. The top must contain structural connections only.

Update bank state and timing history only from committed commands. Enforce tRCD, tRAS, tRP, tRRD, tFAW and tRFC using the selected project profile. A trigger at E permits the blocked command at E+T; tFAW counts earlier ACT commits with age strictly less than its window. Reset creates no synthetic timing history.

Preserve functional banked 32-bit memory and compact host address mapping. WRITE commit updates storage; READ commit at E captures pre-edge data and registers valid/data for host sampling at E+1, with no extra adapter response register. Responses survive active release, cleanup and refresh; writes produce no response.
Open-page retains rows. Support close-page as a configurable alternative, retaining a separate cleanup bank reservation after retirement until a legal PRE commits; block new dispatch during cleanup.

Generate periodic refresh deadlines from the last sampled reset edge using tREFI. Coalesce missed deadlines into sticky pending; a due deadline wins over simultaneous REF acknowledgment. Drain active work and cleanup, PRE remaining open banks in ascending order, respect all-bank tRP, commit REF once, and exclude commands strictly before REF-edge+tRFC. Retain queued traffic and resume service afterward.

cmd_ready is reset-gated diagnostic readiness for the incoming request's first needed command, using independent row/timing probe queries while the engine is idle and cleanup/refresh permit. It is meaningful without txn_valid and must not admit, dispatch, bypass FIFO, mutate history or reserve storage.

Use synchronous active-low reset for state, with immediate valid/ready/event gating. Reset clears queued/active/cleanup work, row state, timing history, memory, responses and refresh state; it wins over every simultaneous event. The host holds payload while stalled and samples every response; no response backpressure is provided.

Generate architecture-specific module isolation and system verification intent with exact requirement IDs, independent scenarios/expected results, and declared port/event bindings. Export it alongside RTL for the external UVM/vector stage. Do not execute downstream verification or backend stages in this frontend flow.

Preserve the existing host ports and widths listed in the baseline contract. Accept a request only on a rising clk edge with txn_valid && txn_ready. Hold payload while stalled. Consecutive accepted cycles with txn_valid held high are distinct requests. cmd_ready is execution/timing visibility, not the host acceptance handshake. Deassert txn_ready and rsp_valid during reset.

Preserve the simplified 4-bit txn_addr mapping: row=txn_addr[3:2], column=txn_addr[1:0], zero-extended into the internal 10-bit row and 6-bit column fields. Preserve explicit txn_bank for multi-bank configurations; a single-bank configuration uses bank 0. Internal packed requests retain bank(2), row(10), column(6), write flag(1), write data(32).

Provide 4 WAITING request slots PLUS one separately stored active-service request: waiting plus active capacity is 5. The active request must not consume a waiting slot. Dispatch captures the complete pre-edge request in active registers and frees its waiting slot without retiring the transaction. A full queue may admit on the same edge as dispatch; retirement alone does not free waiting storage. Accepted request fields survive stalls and each accepted request is serviced exactly once within a reset-free epoch. Keep admission, dispatch, retirement and read response delivery distinct. Captured response storage consumes neither waiting nor active capacity.

Provide functional 32-bit memory storage with 16 addresses per bank, bank isolation and reset-to-zero contents. Accepted writes update only their addressed location at service completion or a committed WRITE. Each accepted read produces exactly one one-cycle rsp_valid pulse with the stored rsp_rdata after read service/READ commit, using the existing one-cycle response stage. Writes produce no host response. Selection and stalled candidates cannot mutate memory; mere command output without storage and read responses is insufficient.

Retain existing tRCD, tRAS and tRP timing protection from the selected JEDEC profile. ACT-to-READ/WRITE must wait tRCD, ACT-to-PRE must respect tRAS, and PRE-to-next-ACT must respect tRP if explicit commands are used. Aggregate service may retain the existing protected timing envelope instead. Configured tRRD and tFAW gates must use accepted activation events, not host admissions or stalled proposals. Never treat existing basic timing as an unrequested future feature.

Dispatch captures the complete selected request in separate active-service registers before freeing its waiting queue slot. Hold that active request and payload across setup PRE/ACT and timing stalls until its final READ/WRITE commits. Setup commands never retire the active request. Aggregate service also keeps active-service ownership through completion. Waiting-queue dequeue at dispatch is distinct from active-request retirement. Row state changes only on the responsible committed operation; uncommitted proposals cannot change state.

Keep request storage, request selection, command sequencing, timing enforcement and functional memory in independently verifiable modules with explicit interfaces. No single controller core may own all these functions. Each mandatory role has distinct module owners with functional inter-module connections. Module names and further decomposition remain design choices.

Compute command permission from registered timing/bank history and an independent candidate. An accepted ACT pulse is derived from candidate && permission; permission must not combinationally depend on that same accepted pulse. Scheduler selection/validity must be available independently of timing_ok; timing_ok may gate commit but must not create a selection-validity feedback loop. Declare accurate per-output combinational input dependencies.

Use top-level clk and active-low rst_n. Reset clears pending requests, active service, row validity, memory and responses. Preserve reusable blocks with either synchronous or asynchronous active-low resets driven by the same rst_n; differing assertion styles do not require rebuilding otherwise reusable blocks. Do not change polarity without an explicit adapter.

Honor the requested scheduler policy fifo. Preserve page policy open_page. Open-page retains a serviced row; close-page closes it before subsequent bank use. Preserve request ownership through any setup sequence. Internal module decomposition and command latency may change while these observable contracts hold.

Retain periodic refresh requests using profile tREFI, refresh priority and request/acknowledgment handling without dropping queued traffic. Refresh must make progress and normal requests must resume. Existing refresh is simplified; full REF/tRFC servicing remains later feature work. If explicit REF is proposed, describe drain/row-state interaction and acknowledge once at commit.
tRRD is enabled; honor that setting and resolve enabled timing values from DDR4-3200.
tFAW is enabled; honor that setting and resolve enabled timing values from DDR4-3200.

READ_RESPONSE_LATENCY.note: A READ committed at edge E captures response state after E for host sampling at E+1.

clock_reset.handshake_gating: Suppress all valid, ready, commit, dispatch, admission, response-delivery, and refresh event conditions while reset is asserted.

admission.condition: Pre-edge txn_valid is high, pre-edge txn_ready is high, and reset is inactive at the rising edge.
admission.effect: Capture exactly one complete mapped request into waiting storage.

dispatch.condition: A previously stored FIFO head is selected, active storage is idle, cleanup is absent, refresh does not forbid dispatch, and reset is inactive at the rising edge.
dispatch.effect: Capture the complete pre-edge FIFO head into active-service storage and release exactly that waiting entry atomically.

command_commit.condition: A non-NOP candidate is present, independently computed permission is true from registered history and bank state, and reset is inactive at the rising edge.
command_commit.effect: Commit at most one command and update only state assigned to that opcode.

retirement.condition: shared.events.command_commit is READ or WRITE for the active request.
retirement.effect: Retire exactly one active request; READ captures response state before active release and WRITE produces no response state.

response_delivery.condition: rsp_valid is high when sampled at a rising edge and reset is inactive.
response_delivery.effect: The host samples rsp_rdata; this event does not alter request capacity.

refresh_due.condition: The periodic deadline is reached at a rising edge with reset inactive.
refresh_due.effect: Set sticky refresh pending; later due events while pending or servicing coalesce.

refresh_start.effect: Acknowledge one pending refresh and begin tRFC command exclusion.

refresh_end.condition: The candidate edge is at least tRFC cycles after a committed REF and reset is inactive.

timing_profile.note: Bindings are resolved from the selected supplied timing-library profile.

timing_rules.edge_convention: A trigger committed at edge E permits a blocked command at edge E+T, never earlier. tFAW counts earlier ACT commits whose age at the candidate edge is strictly less than the tFAW window. Reset creates invalid history and no synthetic timing delay.

SYS_ORDERING.statement: Acceptance order defines global FIFO order. Dispatch transfers only the oldest previously stored request. Physical row state, legality, cleanup, refresh, and timing may delay service but may not select a younger request ahead of the oldest waiting request.

SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.statement: At a reset edge, reset wins over admission, dispatch, command commit, retirement, response delivery, refresh due, and refresh acknowledgment. Without reset, a full waiting queue may admit and dispatch on the same edge using the pre-edge head and pre-edge incoming payload. Retirement does not authorize dispatch on its own edge. A refresh due coincident with REF commit leaves refresh pending set for a later service interval.

SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP.statement: Waiting storage, active-service storage, and captured response storage are logically distinct capacities. Active-service storage contains one complete dispatched request until final READ or WRITE commit. Captured response storage contains no request-capacity claim and survives active release, cleanup, and refresh service.

V_R1.scenario: Apply consecutive valid requests, including same-address writes followed by reads, while command progress varies independently.
V_R1.expected: Each qualifying ready/valid edge admits one request; service and final completion remain in acceptance order; cmd_ready does not affect admission.

V_R2.scenario: Exercise empty, partial, and full waiting storage, including capacity one and simultaneous dispatch/admission.
V_R2.expected: Only pre-edge stored entries dispatch; the pre-edge head is captured before release; no bypass or retirement-edge active replacement occurs.

V_R3.scenario: Service closed-bank, row-hit, and row-conflict reads and writes while timing-blocking each candidate and raising refresh pending.
V_R3.expected: Only NOP, ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF semantics are used; one command at most commits per edge; setup does not retire; blocked candidates remain stable.

V_R4.scenario: Inspect future architecture contracts and interface-level verification intent.
V_R4.expected: Required behavioral roles are independently contractable with structural top-level integration only; no single owner contract contains all required functions.

V_R5.scenario: Test each timing relation at E+T-1 and E+T, including reset, ACT bursts, and REF exclusion.
V_R5.expected: Only committed history changes timing and bank state; tRCD, tRAS, tRP, tRRD, tFAW, and tRFC use the selected profile and exact edge convention.

V_R6.scenario: Write distinct values to all compact addresses in multiple banks, read them, and reset during response visibility.
V_R6.expected: Only committed WRITE changes addressed banked storage; READ captures pre-edge data and produces one E+1 response; responses survive active release and refresh.

V_R7.scenario: Run identical traffic under open_page and close_page parameter values.
V_R7.expected: Open-page retains serviced rows; close-page reserves cleanup until legal PRE and blocks dispatch during cleanup.

V_R8.scenario: Create refresh due conditions while idle, active, cleanup-reserved, and during refresh service; leave multiple banks open.
V_R8.expected: Pending coalesces, due wins over simultaneous acknowledgment, active and cleanup drain before ascending PRE, REF commits once, tRFC exclusion holds, and queued traffic resumes.

V_R9.scenario: Vary incoming address, row state, timing legality, queue fullness, idle/busy state, cleanup, refresh, and txn_valid.
V_R9.expected: cmd_ready reports only the defined first-command diagnostic probe and never changes admission, storage, dispatch, history, or reservations.

V_R10.scenario: Assert reset during queued, active, stalled, refresh, command-commit, and response conditions.
V_R10.expected: Reset immediately gates visible valid, ready, and events low and synchronously clears specified state at the sampled edge; no pre-reset work reappears.

V_R11.scenario: Review generated future verification intent against all rule IDs and declared host/event bindings.
V_R11.expected: Every request rule has reciprocal planned verification, declared independent scenarios, and expected outcomes; no downstream execution claim is made.

V_BASE_HOST.scenario: Hold valid high across ready cycles and hold payload stable across stalls and reset.
V_BASE_HOST.expected: Ports and widths match; each ready/valid edge is distinct; txn_ready and rsp_valid are low during reset; cmd_ready is not an acceptance handshake.

V_BASE_ADDRESS.scenario: Apply every 4-bit address and all four banks.
V_BASE_ADDRESS.expected: Rows and columns are zero-extended from the specified address slices; internal request fields retain bank, row, column, write flag, and data.

V_BASE_QUEUE.scenario: Fill waiting storage while one active request stalls, then perform dispatch/admission, retirement, and read response delivery independently.
V_BASE_QUEUE.expected: Four waiting plus one active request are retained; dispatch frees waiting storage but not transaction ownership; response storage consumes neither capacity.

V_BASE_DATA.scenario: Scoreboard bank-isolated writes and reads over all sixteen locations per bank and inject blocked proposals.
V_BASE_DATA.expected: Reset data are zero; only committed writes update data; every committed read yields exactly one response; proposals do not mutate storage.

V_BASE_TIMING.scenario: Exercise ACT-to-access, ACT-to-PRE, PRE-to-ACT, ACT spacing, and activation-window boundaries.
V_BASE_TIMING.expected: Basic timing remains enforced together with enabled tRRD and tFAW using activation commits rather than admissions or proposals.

V_BASE_SEQUENCE.scenario: Dispatch a complete request, change host inputs afterward, and stall each setup and final command.
V_BASE_SEQUENCE.expected: Captured active payload survives until final commit; dispatch/dequeue and retirement remain distinct; only committed operations change row state.

V_BASE_MODULARITY.scenario: Review future decomposition contracts and declared functional interfaces.
V_BASE_MODULARITY.expected: Request storage, selection, sequencing, timing, and functional memory are independently verifiable and distinct.

V_BASE_LEGALITY.scenario: Independently vary candidate, registered history, selection validity, and timing permission.
V_BASE_LEGALITY.expected: Permission has no same-pulse acceptance feedback; timing may gate commit but cannot create selection-validity feedback; output dependencies are declarable from interface inputs.

V_BASE_RESET.scenario: Check top clock/reset polarity and reset behavior across all state categories.
V_BASE_RESET.expected: clk/rst_n polarity is preserved, synchronous reset clears required state, and no polarity adapter is required.

V_BASE_POLICY.scenario: Compare row-retention and cleanup behavior under configured page-policy values.
V_BASE_POLICY.expected: The default is open_page; close_page behavior remains configurable without loss of request ownership.

V_BASE_REFRESH.scenario: Generate periodic due events under queued traffic and defer service through active work.
V_BASE_REFRESH.expected: Refresh progresses without dropping traffic, acknowledges at REF commit, and normal requests resume.

V_BASE_TRRD.scenario: Commit ACT then attempt another ACT before and at the selected tRRD boundary.
V_BASE_TRRD.expected: The later ACT is blocked before E+tRRD and may proceed at E+tRRD subject to all other permissions.

V_BASE_TFAW.scenario: Inject four earlier ACT commits respecting tRRD and probe a fifth before and at expiration of the oldest tFAW history.
V_BASE_TFAW.expected: The fifth ACT is blocked while four earlier ACTs have age strictly below tFAW and is released when the oldest reaches the boundary subject to other constraints.

V_CONSTRAINT_4.scenario: Inspect refresh behavior and profile bindings.

V_CONSTRAINT_5.scenario: Observe admission, dispatch, and service ordering under row-hit and row-miss traffic.
V_CONSTRAINT_5.expected: FIFO policy is retained independent of row-hit preference.

V_CONSTRAINT_6.scenario: Apply ACT history at the timing boundary.
V_CONSTRAINT_6.expected: tFAW gating is enabled using the selected-profile binding.

V_CONSTRAINT_7.scenario: Apply successive ACT candidates at the timing boundary.
V_CONSTRAINT_7.expected: tRRD gating is enabled using the selected-profile binding.

V_CONSTRAINT_8.scenario: Inspect timing profile selection and command vocabulary.

V_CONSTRAINT_11.scenario: Fill waiting storage under the selected configuration.

V_SYS_ORDERING.scenario: Place older row misses and conflicts ahead of newer row hits and vary timing stalls.
V_SYS_ORDERING.expected: Dispatch and completion follow acceptance order despite different command setup costs.

V_SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.scenario: Align reset, full-queue admission/dispatch, retirement, refresh due, and REF commit in separate and combined trials.
V_SYS_SIMULTANEOUS.expected: Specified priority and same-edge outcomes occur with no lost request, duplicate request, or lost refresh due.

V_SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP.scenario: Track waiting, active, and response occupancy through dispatch, retirement, cleanup, refresh, and response delivery.
V_SYS_STORAGE_OWNERSHIP.expected: The three storage categories remain capacity-independent as specified.

EXEC_COMMANDS.statement: Exactly one non-NOP command may commit at a rising edge. Closed-bank service requires ACT then READ or WRITE; matching open-row service requires READ or WRITE; conflicting open-row service requires PRE then ACT then READ or WRITE. PRE and ACT are setup commands and never retire active service. Candidate payload remains stable while blocked, including when refresh becomes pending.

EXEC_PERMISSION.statement: Candidate selection and validity are independently available before timing permission. Permission is computed from registered bank and timing history and the independent candidate. ACT acceptance equals ACT candidate and permission, but permission has no combinational dependency on the accepted ACT pulse or on same-edge committed command outputs.

EXEC_BANK_STATE.statement: Only committed ACT sets the target bank valid and row, committed PRE clears the target bank validity, and committed REF leaves all banks closed after required preparation. READ and WRITE do not alter row state. Proposals, admissions, dispatch, timing probes, and stalled candidates do not alter row state.

EXEC_CLEANUP.statement: For PAGE_POLICY=open_page, final READ or WRITE retirement retains the serviced row. For PAGE_POLICY=close_page, retirement creates a separate cleanup reservation for the serviced bank; no new dispatch occurs until the required timing-legal PRE commits. Cleanup does not repeat retirement or response delivery.

EXEC_RESPONSE.statement: At READ commit edge E, response storage captures the addressed pre-edge memory word and rsp_valid is asserted after E. The host samples that response at E+1. In the absence of replacement, rsp_valid clears after the delivery edge while rsp_rdata may retain its last value. A delivery and a new READ commit may share an edge: old response data is delivered before new response state replaces it. WRITE produces no response.

EXEC_REFRESH.statement: Refresh deadlines are measured from the last sampled reset edge. The first due edge is E0+tREFI and later deadlines advance by tREFI independently of REF commit. Pending is sticky and coalesces later due edges. Once pending is visible, no new dispatch occurs; active service and required cleanup complete, then open banks PRE in ascending bank order, respecting timing. REF commits once after all banks are closed and all-bank tRP is satisfied. Commands are excluded at candidate edges strictly before REF-edge+tRFC; queued traffic remains retained and resumes after service when no pending refresh remains.

V_EXEC_COMMANDS.scenario: Run closed, hit, and conflict sequences with multi-cycle timing stalls and refresh pending transitions.
V_EXEC_COMMANDS.expected: Committed trace is ACT-access, access, or PRE-ACT-access as applicable; setup never retires and no candidate changes while blocked.

V_EXEC_PERMISSION.scenario: Probe permission with fixed registered history while varying candidate and compare against stalled and accepted ACT behavior.
V_EXEC_PERMISSION.expected: Candidate validity remains independently observable; permission is history-based and acceptance feedback-free.

V_EXEC_BANK_STATE.scenario: Commit ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, and REF in multiple banks and separately issue uncommitted proposals.
V_EXEC_BANK_STATE.expected: Only responsible committed commands change only permitted bank-state fields.

V_EXEC_CLEANUP.scenario: Retire accesses under both page policies and raise refresh during close-page cleanup.
V_EXEC_CLEANUP.expected: Open-page retains rows; close-page reserves cleanup and blocks dispatch until PRE commits without duplicate retirement or response.

V_EXEC_RESPONSE.scenario: Commit reads on adjacent edges, read after writes, issue writes, and reset during a response pulse.
V_EXEC_RESPONSE.expected: Each read returns captured pre-edge data exactly once at E+1, writes return no response, and old data is delivered before same-edge replacement.

V_EXEC_REFRESH.scenario: Observe first due from reset, delayed REF, coincident due/REF, multiple open banks, and post-tRFC restart.
V_EXEC_REFRESH.expected: Deadlines do not drift, pending is sticky and coalesced, preparation ordering is ascending, REF is singular, and exclusion ends exactly at E+tRFC.

handshakes.admission: shared.events.admission occurs only from pre-edge txn_valid and txn_ready while reset is inactive. enqueue_valid represents txn_valid; queue_ready supplies admission backpressure.
handshakes.response: Pass the memory-owned registered response stage directly to rsp_valid and rsp_rdata without another response register.
handshakes.diagnostic: cmd_ready is probe_ready only. It does not affect txn_ready, enqueue_valid, request storage, dispatch, timing history, or reservation.

host_protocol.reset: Immediately gate enqueue_valid, txn_ready, cmd_ready, and rsp_valid low while rst_n is low. rsp_rdata is zero while reset is asserted. This module owns no state.
host_protocol.stalls: The mapped request is combinationally available from host payload fields. The host stability requirement applies while txn_valid is asserted and txn_ready is low.

simultaneous_events.admission_and_response: Admission and response delivery are independent.
simultaneous_events.reset_and_events: Reset wins and gates all visible handshake events.

host_protocol.dependency_note: shared reset gating is implicit in every visible output.

owned_state.entries: FIFO-ordered shared.types.request entries, with configurable capacity shared.parameters.WAITING_CAPACITY.
owned_state.occupancy: Registered count of waiting entries only; active and response storage are excluded.

handshakes.dispatch: Remove only the pre-edge head on shared.events.dispatch; head_take alone is not an event.
handshakes.readiness: enqueue_ready is true when pre-edge occupancy is below capacity or a valid pre-edge head dispatches on this edge.

waiting_queue.reset: Synchronously clear all waiting entries and occupancy; immediately gate enqueue_ready and head_valid low during reset. Invalid head_request is canonical zero.

update_events.shared.events.admission: Append the complete pre-edge enqueue_request after all older waiting entries.
update_events.shared.events.dispatch: Capture and remove only the pre-edge FIFO head. Simultaneous admission appends after that old head is removed.

waiting_queue.stalls: Stored entries and head_request remain stable until dispatch or reset. A tail admission cannot change a stalled head.

simultaneous_events.full_enqueue_and_dispatch: The pre-edge head is removed and the incoming request becomes the newest entry; occupancy is unchanged, including capacity one.
simultaneous_events.retirement_and_enqueue: Retirement does not change waiting occupancy or readiness.

handshakes.selection: dispatch_valid reflects the previously stored FIFO head independently of timing permission and dispatch_ready.
handshakes.dispatch: shared.events.dispatch occurs when dispatch_valid and dispatch_ready are both high. head_take follows that condition.

fifo_scheduler.reset: Immediately gate dispatch_valid and head_take low during reset. No owned state exists.
fifo_scheduler.stalls: Continue exposing the same FIFO head while dispatch_ready is low; this module never selects a younger row hit.

simultaneous_events.admission_and_dispatch: Selection uses the pre-edge queue head; insertion handling belongs to waiting_queue.
simultaneous_events.retirement_and_dispatch: The engine keeps dispatch_ready low on retirement edges under the recorded no-same-edge-replacement decision.

owned_state.active_request: One complete dispatched shared.types.request retained until committed READ or WRITE.
owned_state.candidate: Registered non-NOP command proposal and validity held unchanged while permission is false.
owned_state.cleanup: Optional close-page cleanup bank reservation retained after retirement until committed PRE.
owned_state.refresh_preparation: Registered ascending-bank preparation cursor and phase; it is distinct from refresh pending/service state.

handshakes.dispatch: shared.events.dispatch captures the complete pre-edge dispatch_request before queue storage is released. Timing permission never gates dispatch.
handshakes.commit: shared.events.command_commit is candidate_valid and candidate_ok. commit_valid is never asserted for NOP.
handshakes.probe: Probe independently derives the incoming request first needed command while idle and permitted by cleanup/refresh state. It has no state-changing effect.

command_engine.reset: Synchronously clear active, candidate, cleanup, and preparation ownership. Immediately gate dispatch_ready, candidate_valid, commit_valid, probe_valid, and probe_ready low. Invalid command outputs are canonical NOP.

update_events.shared.events.dispatch: Capture the complete pre-edge head into active storage and defer first candidate formation until a later edge.
update_events.shared.events.command_commit: Committed PRE or ACT advances setup only. Committed READ or WRITE retires active ownership; close_page creates cleanup ownership and open_page retains row ownership. Committed REF completes refresh preparation.
update_events.every_clock: When no blocked candidate exists, form a candidate from registered active, cleanup, or refresh-preparation ownership. Once refresh_pending is visible, prevent new dispatch, drain active and cleanup, precharge open banks in ascending order, then propose REF. No dispatch occurs while refresh_busy is high.

command_engine.stalls: A valid candidate and complete active payload remain unchanged while candidate_ok is low, including when refresh_pending becomes visible. New candidate formation occurs only after a prior candidate commits.

simultaneous_events.refresh_due_and_final_access: The final access may commit; newly visible pending blocks subsequent dispatch and preparation begins later.
simultaneous_events.refresh_due_and_REF: REF acknowledgment does not erase simultaneous due; refresh control retains pending.
simultaneous_events.retirement_and_dispatch: dispatch_ready is low when active ownership exists before the edge; retirement cannot cause same-edge replacement.

owned_state.open_rows: Registered row value for each bank.
owned_state.open_valid: Registered open-row validity for each bank.

bank_state.reset: Synchronously clear all row-valid and row fields; immediately gate open_valid low during reset.

update_events.shared.events.command_commit: Committed ACT sets only its target bank valid and row. Committed PRE clears only its target bank valid. Committed REF leaves all banks closed after required preparation. READ and WRITE do not change row state.

bank_state.stalls: No command proposal, permission query, admission, dispatch, or blocked candidate mutates bank state.

simultaneous_events.command_commit: Only one committed command is permitted per edge.

owned_state.bank_history: Registered ACT and PRE histories per bank.
owned_state.global_history: Registered ACT spacing history, up to four unexpired ACT timestamps for tFAW, and REF exclusion history.

handshakes.permission: Evaluate candidate and probe independently from registered history, registered row state, and query command. Invalid, NOP, reserved, bank-illegal, or timing-illegal queries return false.
handshakes.history: Only shared.events.command_commit inserts ACT, PRE, or REF history. Permission has no combinational dependency on commit_valid or any accepted ACT pulse.

timing_enforcement.reset: Synchronously invalidate all histories and immediately gate candidate_ok and probe_ok low during reset.

update_events.every_clock: Age and expire histories using the locked edge convention while idle or stalled; elapsed time alone creates no history.
update_events.shared.events.command_commit: Committed ACT updates tRCD, tRAS, tRRD, and tFAW histories; committed PRE updates tRP history; committed REF starts tRFC exclusion.

timing_enforcement.stalls: Blocked proposals do not insert, refresh, or otherwise alter timing history.

simultaneous_events.expiration_and_commit: Permission is evaluated against earlier registered history at the candidate edge; a committed trigger is inserted after that decision.
simultaneous_events.probe_and_commit: Probe observes pre-edge history and is not changed by same-edge commit.

owned_state.words: Four isolated banks of sixteen 32-bit words.
owned_state.response: One registered response valid/data stage separate from waiting and active capacity.

handshakes.commit: Observe broadcast shared.events.command_commit. Only committed WRITE mutates storage; only committed READ captures response state.
handshakes.response: shared.events.response_delivery samples the registered response. No response-ready or response backpressure exists.

memory_responses.reset: Synchronously zero all words, response validity, and response data. Immediately gate rsp_valid low during reset.

update_events.shared.events.command_commit: WRITE updates exactly its addressed bank and compact address. READ captures the addressed pre-edge word into response storage. Other commands do not mutate memory or response state.
update_events.shared.events.response_delivery: Clear response valid unless a simultaneous committed READ replaces response state after old response delivery.

memory_responses.stalls: Candidates, probes, selection, and noncommitted commands cannot mutate storage. Captured response state survives active release, cleanup, and refresh.

simultaneous_events.response_delivery_and_READ: Deliver old response data, then capture the new pre-edge read word for the next edge.
simultaneous_events.response_delivery_and_WRITE: Deliver old response independently; WRITE creates no response.

owned_state.deadline: Periodic deadline measured from the last sampled reset edge.
owned_state.service: Registered REF service exclusion state through tRFC.

handshakes.request: shared.events.refresh_due sets sticky pending and advances the deadline by tREFI independently of REF commit.
handshakes.acknowledgment: shared.events.refresh_start, a committed REF, is the sole acknowledgment and starts tRFC service exclusion.

refresh_control.reset: Synchronously clear pending, service, and deadline state; rebase the first deadline at the sampled reset edge. Immediately gate outputs low during reset.

update_events.shared.events.refresh_due: Set pending and advance periodic deadline. A due event while pending or servicing coalesces.
update_events.shared.events.refresh_start: Clear pending unless refresh_due also occurs at the edge; start service exclusion.
update_events.shared.events.refresh_end: End service exclusion while retaining any independently pending refresh.

refresh_control.stalls: Pending persists through active work, cleanup, timing stalls, and service. This module owns no waiting request storage.

simultaneous_events.due_and_REF: Due wins pending update; REF starts service and one later refresh remains pending.
simultaneous_events.due_and_service_end: Service may end but pending remains set.

graph.integration: The top is structural only. Shared clk and rst_n are implicit child inputs through shared.clock_reset; all other functional connectivity is explicit typed whole-port wiring.

refresh_due.reason: The periodic deadline is owned internally by refresh_control. Downstream checking derives due edges from reset and shared timing profile and observes refresh_pending independently.

refresh_end.reason: No public end pulse exists. Downstream checking derives the tRFC boundary from committed REF and observes refresh_busy independently.
